page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the c2d server family. It features 16 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. The processor supports hardware-level features such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX), AES and VAES cryptography, SHA_NI, and hyper-threading, though it lacks AVX-512 support.

In benchmark evaluations, the c2d-highcpu-16 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, scoring 2926.98 in stress-ng tests, which places it in the top 25% of tested instances. Passmark memory testing also registers a strong score of 2765.98. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23457.88 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10397.0, both falling within the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 80.47 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 48.72 GB/sec for writes. For small-model LLM inference of 135M parameters, text generation speed is strong at 301.82 tokens/sec, while prompt processing is average at 1262.4 tokens/sec.

The instance does not include local NVMe storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring external block storage attachment. This resource profile offers high compute density relative to memory capacity, making it a cost-efficient option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, static web serving, text and image processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. With 8 physical cores and a 2.0 GB per core memory ratio, this instance is designed for compute-heavy workloads. It exhibits strong single-core CPU performance and strong memory scores in Passmark benchmarks, alongside strong text generation speeds for small LLM models. However, its multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average tier. The server lacks local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, presenting a tradeoff for storage-intensive applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for high-compute, low-memory tasks, making it suitable for software compilation, static web serving, and image processing.
